correctness.rationale: A direct arclength-consecutive-gap and cap-area Fubini identity gives an exact determinant kernel. Rectangle tangent enumeration yields the evaluated closed expression for every n>=2, with affine angle reduction. An explicit strictly convex one-dimensional kernel proves all-n strict ordering and equality conditions; direct endpoint computations prove both bounds. Dominated convergence supplies the thin-shape limit and exponential asymptotics the fixed-shape limit. Twenty-eight exact rational comparisons with an independently expanded integral and six sheared convex-hull simulations corroborate, without replacing, the proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected direct boundary-polytope paper proves fixed-shape missing-volume asymptotics; its exact all-finite-n side-ratio extremum and singular n*u->tau limit are not among its stated results. The Hausdorff paper has a different loss. The nearest accessible preceding area-hull result yields only a leading fixed-weight term and an approximate finite sample expression. General old integral expressions create residual priority risk, but no source examined was found to imply the complete new theorem.
residual_risks: Historical equivalence may exist in older integral-geometry or random-polygon sources not accessible in full, notably Efron (1965).
A general expectation identity could recover the finite-n expression by specialization, although no inspected source stated its sharp all-n extremal/degenerate aspect conclusions.
The mathematical priority conclusion is best-knowledge, not an independent exhaustive literature certification.

value.rationale: The theorem solves the natural fixed-sample expectation for all Euclidean parallelograms, including exact rhombus-only extremality and inverse identification of side ratio. Its n*u->tau transition is a meaningful, nonuniform phenomenon showing how a collapsing short edge changes the approximation rate from n^-2 to n^-1; this cannot be recovered from only fixed-aspect leading terms. The closed formula is not just an unmotivated single numerical case.
